units: <cite ref="Bava Kamma 80a">B. Kam. 80ᵃ</cite> <he>שרצא ה׳</he> Ms. M. (ed. <cite ref="H01753"><he>חרצא</he></cite>) a prickly creeping animal, v. <cite ref="H01648"><he>חרְזָא</he></cite>.

senses.gloss: the long and thin foliage of a palm-branch spreading from the stem.
units: Succ. 32ᵃ a Lulab דסליק בחד ה׳ which spreads its foliage on one side only.—Pl. הוּצֵי.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 96a:10">B. Kam. 96ᵃ</cite> if one stole a palm-branch <he>ועבדינהו ה׳</he> and tore it into leaves.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 92a:17">B. Kam. 92ᵃ</cite> (prov.) <he>בהדי ה׳ לקי כרבא</he> with the shrub the cabbage is smitten (the good suffer with the bad).
<cite ref="Nedarim 49b:6">Ned. 49ᵇ</cite> <he>אכיל בה׳</he> ate with a thorn (as a fork).
<cite ref="Nedarim 91b:3-7">Ib. 91ᵇ</cite> <he>פרטיה … לה׳ וכ׳</he> the lover parted the hedge and ran off.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 4a:10">B. Bath. 4ᵃ</cite> <he>דנהיגי בה׳ ודפנא</he> where it is customary to make fences with shrubbery or bay-trees.—
<cite ref="Bava Batra 4b:6">Ib. 4ᵇ</cite> <he>ה׳ לית ליה וכ׳</he> where they use hedges for fences, the exclusive ownership of one neighbor can only be secured by a deed.—Pl. <he>הוּצֵי</he>.
